findings.reason: the section should name `seat_names_a_live_foreign_producer` so the watcher wait and the snapshot producer share one foreign-seat judgement instead of two.
findings.text: §2 says the foreign-seat judgement "reuses `_seat_names_a_foreign_host` and `_seat_stream_fresh`", but `seat_names_a_live_foreign_producer(project)` already composes exactly that judgement (a seat naming a foreign host whose stream is fresh) and is already the single reader used for this purpose by the obligation snapshot producer (`reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:313`, via `_foreign_seat_is_live`). Re-composing the two primitives inside the watch loop forks the judgement into a second spelling that can drift from the snapshot producer's; and §4 says "the hook on any host reads it through the same foreign-seat judgement as §2", which only holds if §2 names the composite rather than a fresh composition.

findings.reason: citing `watch_observer_alive` as the precedent fixes the "for example from a stamp the follower refreshes" question §4 leaves open and keeps the two host-blindness rules consistent.
findings.text: §4's rule "a registration naming another host is never put to this host's process table" already exists as an implemented pattern: `watch_observer_alive` returns `None` (unknown, not dead) for a registration naming a foreign host, precisely so a local reader does not judge a peer host's pid. The plan introduces the same rule for the follower registration without citing it, so the two cross-host liveness rules are written independently and the follower rule must re-solve what the watcher rule already settled (returning unknown rather than dead).

findings.reason: naming the owner — add a unit-property reader to `SystemdUserUnitManager` and reach it through the `manager` seam `ensure_watcher_service` already exposes (`reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:381`) — keeps one systemd client and lets the existing watch tests supply a fake manager.
findings.text: §5 delivers "`reckon crew watch --ensure` reads the unit's restart count twice" but names no source for that count and no module to own it. The owner of every systemd unit query in reckon is `SystemdUserUnitManager` (`reckon/service.py:324`), whose `active()` (`reckon/service.py:341`) already shells `systemctl --user is-active`; the newcomer in the incident (restart count 2,376, `ExecMainStatus=0`) is not read anywhere in the tree (no `NRestarts`/`systemctl show` reader exists). Placing the restart read in the watch path makes the watch module a second systemd client beside the manager, with its own error handling.

findings.reason: the plan's census names two of six consumers; the author must check the semantics of `watch_state`/`session_host`/`dispatch_watch` before flipping a foreign registration to `live`, because a dispatch guard that now reads a remote follower as delivering turns a refusal into an admission.
findings.text: census: §4 changes liveness at its single reader, `_follower_liveness` (`reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:506-517`, `record_process_alive` + local `process_alive(parent_pid)`), and names two consumers — the obligation producer (`reckon/crew/runs.py:2164`) and the review reflex (`reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2557`). Six readers depend on the same `live` value and flip together: `reckon/crew/runs.py:2164`, `reckon/crew/runs.py:2795` (`project_watch_visibility`), `reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:170` (`watch_state`, feeding dispatch admission), `reckon/crew/session_host.py:421` (`_foreign_live_follower`), `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:720` (peer-delivery listing), and `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2557`. Two of the unnamed four are guards, not reports: `watch_state`'s `attached`/`session_attached` feeds dispatch admission (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:708-720`), and `session_host._foreign_live_follower` decides whether a live follower this host did not start holds the pair — each of these would begin counting a remote follower as delivering.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 and §4 extend existing machinery in place (the watcher follow loop; the single `_follower_liveness` reader) rather than adding a parallel module, and §4 explicitly funnels both consumers through one liveness change.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 introduces a systemd unit-property read (restart count) without naming `SystemdUserUnitManager` (`reckon/service.py:324`) as the owner of unit queries, and §4's account names two of the six consumers of the liveness reader it changes.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1721, cli_options 349, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; no reviewed section adds a CLI option, MCP view, public definition or refusal family — §2 and §5 change the behaviour and the payload of existing commands (`crew watch`, `crew watch --ensure`), and §4 adds a data field (`host`) to the follower registration, not a new interface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the watch/seat code and cites real helpers, but §2 re-composes a foreign-seat judgement that already exists whole (`seat_names_a_live_foreign_producer`, `reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:143`), and §4 re-derives a cross-host liveness rule already established by `watch_observer_alive` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:2710`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section adds a forwarding layer; §5's restart-count read is an extension of the `--ensure` path, not a wrapper over existing machinery.
